Title: Trial defence says Russia used Nord Stream pipelines as 'weapon'
Article:
HAMBURG: A lawyer for a Ukrainian accused of blowing up the Nord Stream pipelines supplying Russian gas to western Europe said on Wednesday that Moscow had used the network to exert political and economic pressure, as the former military officer's trial opened in Germany.
Sergiy Kuznietsov is the first person to go on trial over the 2022 sabotage. The 50-year-old is accused of leading a Ukrainian team of divers and an explosives expert to bomb Nord Stream, seven months after Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine.
Prosecutor Stefan Schmidt told the Hamburg court that Kuznietsov, acting on behalf of the Ukrainian state, had committed a war crime by "using military means" to hit civilian targets.
He is also charged with attacking civilian infrastructure and causing an explosion.
Defence lawyer Nicola Canestrini told the court there was no clear evidence linking the former special forces officer to the sabotage.
He also accused Russia of using the pipelines as a political and economic "weapon".
Russia had exerted immense pressure on Germany at the time, and gas markets went haywire before Moscow turned off the tap.
"In September 2022, the pipelines were not supplying anyone with heat," Canestrini said.
"They were a means of exerting pressure in a war," he added, saying Russia, rather than his client, was guilty of committing war crimes.
Dwindling gas supplies
Three of the four pipelines were seriously damaged by the blasts under the Baltic Sea in September 2022.
Before the sabotage rendered them inoperable, Russia had steadily reduced gas supplies through the pipelines to Europe, apparently in retaliation for sanctions imposed over its invasion.
While some in the West were quick to accuse Russia of sabotaging its own export route, German investigators identified a cell of Ukrainians they said were the alleged perpetrators.
According to the indictment, Kuznietsov entered Germany in early September 2022 using a forged Ukrainian passport and, together with the rest of the sabotage team, boarded a rented yacht in the German Baltic Sea port city of Rostock.
The yacht was allegedly loaded with large quantities of military-grade explosives and set sail for a spot where the pipelines ran under the Baltic Sea near the Danish island of Bornholm.
Divers then allegedly planted explosive charges equipped with timers on the pipelines, which blew up several days later.
Prosecutor Schmidt said the bombing aimed to ensure deliveries through the pipelines would be "permanently halted", so Russia could no longer use revenue from gas sales to finance its war efforts.
[[nid:1555738]]
'What are war crimes?'
The defendant will not testify during the trial, with his lawyers saying confidentiality rules prevent former Ukrainian special forces personnel from speaking publicly about their activities.
The pipelines were built and owned by a corporate consortium led by Russian energy giant Gazprom.
At the time of the blasts, none were in operation.
Moscow had already suspended gas deliveries to western Europe through Nord Stream 1, which comprised two pipelines.
Nord Stream 2, also made up of two pipelines, had just been completed and never entered service.
Kyiv has consistently denied orchestrating the sabotage but has made no secret of its satisfaction with the results.
Another suspect, partially identified as Volodymyr Z., was arrested in Croatia in August and is accused of taking part in the sabotage as a diver.
A Croatian court has approved his extradition to Germany, although he is appealing the decision.
Late on Wednesday, the suspect's Croatian lawyer, Ivan Grzic, said his client had sought political asylum there.
The Interior Ministry would determine whether Croatia had jurisdiction over the case, he said.
If so, the Ukrainian would be interviewed and asked to provide relevant documents, the lawyer added.
Since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine, Germany has become Kyiv's leading military backer and regularly accuses Russia of sabotage and espionage on its soil.
The investigation into the Nord Stream sabotage has proved awkward for diplomatic ties, but German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul noted on Wednesday that President Volodymyr Zelenskyy had said Ukraine was not responsible.
"I am waiting for the outcome of these proceedings, and then the government will take a position," he said.
Ukraine's supporters in Germany have also been unhappy with the trial, however, and a small group protested outside the Hamburg court on Wednesday.
They held placards reading: "Russia is a terrorist" and "What are war crimes? A blown-up pipeline? Or the bombing of buildings and the killing of people?"

Title: MinDef enters cooperation with HR Ministry on veteran employment
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 15 — The Ministry of Defence (MinDef) is strengthening its commitment to the welfare and future of Malaysian Armed Forces (MAF) personnel and veterans through the MyBakat Veteran initiative, which aims to benefit more than 15,000 people by 2030.
Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said the initiative underscores MinDef’s new approach to ensuring that MAF personnel receive support not only during their service but are also better prepared to pursue a second career after retirement.
He said the ministry is placing greater emphasis on aligning military skills and experience with industry requirements to broaden job opportunities for MAF personnel and veterans.
“We are moving away from the ‘train first, find a job later’ approach towards directly matching personnel’s competencies with industry needs, relevant training and actual career opportunities,” he said.
He said this at the signing of a Note of Cooperation between MinDef and the Ministry of Human Resources to implement MyBakat Veteran here yesterday.
MinDef secretary-general Datuk Lokman Hakim Ali and HR Ministry secretary-general Datuk Azman Mohd Yusof signed the Note of Cooperation in the presence of Mohamed Khaled and Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan.
Also present was Chief of Defence Force General Tan Sri Malek Razak Sulaiman.
A memorandum of understanding (MoU) was also signed by MinDef, the Armed Forces Ex-Servicemen Affairs Corporation (PERHEBAT) and the Malaysian Employers Federation (MEF) to facilitate the placement of PERHEBAT trainees and MAF veterans with companies under MEF for a six-month transition period before they are absorbed into permanent positions.
Mohamed Khaled said the initiative focuses on career preparation at least two years before retirement, noting that between 5,000 and 7,000 MAF personnel leave the service each year.
“The strategic collaboration also offers opportunities for military experience and expertise to be recognised as professional qualifications through the Malaysian Skills Certificate (SKM) and Malaysian Skills Diploma (DKM), subject to competency assessments and eligibility criteria.
“It also strengthens the roles of PERHEBAT and the Malaysian Armed Forces Veterans Affairs Department (JHEV), with support from TalentCorp and relevant agencies, in providing career transition training and access to job opportunities,” he said.
He said the collaboration highlights MinDef’s efforts to expand the support ecosystem for MAF personnel through a more structured, integrated approach that responds to labour market needs. — Bernama

Title: Zara Qairina inquest: Coroner concludes witness phase, to set final directions tomorrow
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Oct 15 — The Coroner’s Court here today concluded hearing the testimonies of all 83 witnesses in the inquest into the death of Zara Qairina Mahathir, with Coroner Amir Shah Amir Hassan fixing Friday morning for further directions on submissions.
Amir Shah, before adjourning today’s proceedings, said no further deponents would be called on Friday, with the court sitting at 9 am for directions on submissions in the inquest into the death of Zara Qairina.
“On Friday, I will hear from the parties and decide on the directions for submissions,” he said.
The coroner said the grounds for the verdict would be delivered in Bahasa Malaysia to make the inquest findings easier to understand.
Zara Qairina died at Queen Elizabeth Hospital on July 17, 2025, a day after she was found unconscious near a drain at her school hostel in the early hours of July 16.
On Aug 13, 2025, the Attorney General’s Chambers (AGC) announced that an inquest would be conducted into Zara Qairina’s death after reviewing the investigation report submitted by police.
On Aug 8, 2025, the AGC said that Zara Qairina’s remains would be exhumed to allow for a post-mortem examination.
The exhumation at the Tanjung Ubi Muslim Cemetery, Kampung Mesapol, Sipitang, was completed at 7.15 pm on Aug 9, 2025.
The inquest into the death of the Form One student commenced on Sept 13 last year. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia is building its own digital cloud to safeguard data sovereignty, minister says
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 15 — The government is developing a sovereign artificial intelligence (AI) cloud to ensure the country’s classified information remains secure and beyond the reach of foreign laws and policies, said Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil.
He said the initiative was crucial to protecting Malaysia’s digital sovereignty, particularly in securing sensitive government information, including official documents, that could be at risk if stored on public cloud services.
“Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim previously mentioned this initiative, which we are now in the process of implementing. It is vital for our digital sovereignty, which is the sovereign cloud.
“We have observed that some countries have policies and laws that could make the use of public clouds less secure, especially when it comes to classified information. Therefore, the government has decided to develop a sovereign AI cloud,” he said.
Fahmi was speaking as a guest on Bernama TV Ruang Bicara programme, titled “Budget 2027: Empowering Communication, Driving the Orange Economy”, here yesterday.
He said the initiative would be managed by the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) and the Communications Ministry.
Meanwhile, Fahmi said providing wider, faster, more affordable and secure Internet access was crucial to strengthening the country’s digital economy, which is estimated to contribute more than 25.5 per cent to gross domestic product (GDP).
He said Phase One of the National Digital Network (JENDELA) initiative had helped bridge the Internet access gap between urban and rural areas. However, connectivity challenges remained, particularly when users travelled beyond village areas.
“The issue arises when someone leaves a village and suddenly loses the signal. We need to ensure that connectivity remains uninterrupted,” he said.
He added that improved Internet connectivity would benefit entrepreneurs selling products online, students participating in digital learning, and members of the public accessing information or applying for government services online.
Fahmi said 5G technology could also improve efficiency in the agricultural sector through the use of the Internet of Things (IoT) and robotics.
Under Budget 2027, the government has allocated RM5 billion for JENDELA to expand high-quality Internet coverage, particularly in rural and remote areas. — Bernama

Title: Religious minister urges joint Muslim prayers as ‘weapon’ against haze
Article:

solat hajat

Title: Finance Ministry: RON97 down to RM5.10, diesel to RM5.17
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 15 — The retail prices of RON97 and unsubsidised RON95 petrol will fall by 5 sen per litre each to RM5.10 and RM4.62 respectively, while unsubsidised diesel will drop by 10 sen to RM5.17 per litre from Oct 15 to 21.
In a statement yesterday, the Ministry of Finance (MOF) said although Brent crude oil prices remained above US$100 (RM409) per barrel, supplies of refined petroleum products in the regional market had begun to show signs of recovery.
According to the ministry, China had re-authorised fuel exports for October, while South Korea continued to supply refined petroleum products to the regional market, helping to ease supply pressures.
“Nevertheless, the conflict in West Asia, including the attacks in Saudi Arabia last week, increases the risk of supply disruptions and rising petroleum prices. Price volatility is expected to continue in the medium term.
“The government will continue to protect the people and businesses from the impact of this global uncertainty. As announced in Budget 2027, the government is expected to spend RM40 billion on fuel subsidies next year to support economic growth and ensure the sustainability of the people’s livelihoods,” MOF said.
MOF said recipients of BUDI MADANI RON95 (BUDI95) would continue to pay RM1.99 per litre, compared with the unsubsidised RON95 price of RM4.62 per litre. The government would bear a subsidy of RM2.63 per litre, or 57 per cent of the unsubsidised price.
Recipients of BUDI MADANI Diesel (BUDI Diesel) would continue to pay RM2.10 per litre, compared with the unsubsidised diesel price of RM5.17 per litre. The government would provide a subsidy of RM3.07 per litre, or 59 per cent of the unsubsidised price.
“Although the country’s fuel supply remains sufficient for now, the government urges the public to continue practising prudent fuel consumption.
“More efficient travel planning and reducing unnecessary trips can help prolong the nation’s fuel supply and reduce pressure on subsidy expenditure,” the ministry said.
MOF said the government would continue to take a prudent approach to protect the people from price fluctuations while ensuring that the country’s fuel supply remained sufficient and secure. — Bernama

Title: Fahmi: Pakatan 95pc done with Melaka candidate talks
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 15 — Discussions on the list of Pakatan Harapan (PH) candidates for the Melaka state election are over 95 per cent complete, said PH Communications director Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil.
Fahmi, who is also communications minister, said PH has scheduled its candidate announcement for Oct 24, with the venue to be confirmed later.
“
Insya-Allah
, the candidates who will represent Pakatan Harapan will be announced on Oct 24. Discussions at the party level are now more than 90 to 95 per cent complete,” he told Bernama here yesterday.
Fahmi said discussions on the candidate list begin at the PH component-party level, after which the party contesting a particular seat can hold talks with other parties, if necessary.
“If any party entrusted with contesting a particular seat sees a need to discuss the matter with other parties, it is up to them to do so, and ultimately, the final decision will be made by the Pakatan Harapan Presidential Council,” he added.
Meanwhile, Fahmi said the candidate announcement, originally scheduled for today, had been postponed to Oct 24 at the request of the Melaka PH leadership.
He said the change was not due to any permit issues involving the local authorities or problems with the event venue.
“No… the date was rescheduled at the request of several leaders, including our Pakatan Harapan colleagues in Melaka.
“So, we rescheduled it, and Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, who is also PH chairman, is expected to attend on Oct 24,” he added.
Previously, the media reported that the candidate announcement and launch of the PH election machinery for the 16th Melaka state election, scheduled for Sunday (Oct 18), had been postponed.
The postponement raised questions after allegations emerged on social media linking the date change to difficulties in obtaining a local authority permit for the event venue. — Bernama

Title: In Dewan Rakyat today: Haze, electricity tariffs, and data centres
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 15 — The Dewan Rakyat is expected to discuss several key issues today, including increases in domestic electricity tariffs, the economic value of data centre investments, aviation safety and the impact of haze on public health.
According to the Order Paper on Parliament’s official portal, during the Minister’s Question Time, Azli Yusof (PH-Shah Alam) will seek an explanation from the Minister of Energy Transition and Water Transformation on the factors behind the increase in domestic electricity charges and the Energy Commission’s assurance that about 85 per cent of households would be shielded from the impact of the adjustment through the Energy Efficiency Incentive.
Datuk Wan Hassan Mohd Ramli (PN-Dungun) will ask about the Youth and Sports Ministry’s assessment of the Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix 2026 at the Sepang International Circuit, covering the event’s effectiveness, operational preparedness, stakeholder coordination and proposed improvements.
Meanwhile, Datuk Dr Richard Rapu @ Aman Begri (GPS-Betong) will ask the Transport Minister to clarify the safety audit records, monitoring audits and latest inspection carried out by the Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM) on the operator of helicopter 80-105 9M-LLF following the crash in Long Lellang.
During the Oral Question-and-Answer session, Rodziah Ismail (PH-Ampang) will ask how the net value added by data centre investments is measured after accounting for resource use, incentives, employment, local content and the country’s opportunity costs, following the approval of RM385.7 billion in investments since 2021.
Cha Kee Chin (PH-Rasah) will ask about the Health Ministry’s measures to address the impact of haze on public health, including cooperation with the Department of Environment and relevant agencies to monitor air quality, issue health advisories, and protect vulnerable groups.
Chong Chieng Jen (PH-Stampin) will seek an update on the growing misuse of synthetic drugs in Sarawak and the effectiveness of measures taken by the Royal Malaysia Police, while Shaharizukirnain Abd Kadir (PN-Setiu) will ask about proposed amendments to the Environmental Quality Act 1974 to enable companies and importers that repeatedly violate laws on illegal electronic waste to be blacklisted.
Meanwhile, Datuk Willie Mongin (GPS-Puncak Borneo) will ask about efforts to strengthen the legal and policy framework for national unity when dealing with sensitive issues involving religion, race and the royal institution (3R), including a proposal to introduce a comprehensive National Unity Act.
The Dewan Rakyat sitting will then proceed with the first reading of the Adoption (Amendment) Bill 2026, followed by the fourth day of debate on the Supply Bill (Budget) 2027.
The Dewan Rakyat sitting runs for 37 days until Dec 8. — Bernama

Title: How Malaysia can raise its retirement age from 60 to 65: Experts explain the math and more
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 15 — Should Malaysia push its retirement age up from 60 to 65, and if yes, how can it be done?
Currently, Malaysia’s minimum retirement age of 60 means private sector employees are protected from premature retirement before 60, while civil servants have a mandatory retirement age of 60.
However, global pension expert William Price said Malaysia needs to gradually increase its retirement age to at least 65 as Malaysians are living longer.
He said “it’s very strange that Malaysia’s retirement age has been so low for so long” when many other countries had increased theirs.
“Usually some countries do it in a crisis period where suddenly they have to increase it very rapidly and that’s tough,” he told
Malay Mail
at the sidelines of the Employees Provident Fund’s (EPF) International Social Wellbeing Conference (ISWC) 2026.
He explained that people may find it psychologically difficult to accept if the retirement age is suddenly raised, such as when a 59-year-old person thought they were one year away from retirement, but are suddenly told they have to work six years more before retiring at 65.
“But also it’s just difficult for you in terms of your life and employer, you might not have prepared for it,” the CEO of consultancy firm D3P Global Pension Consulting said.
“So countries have a gradual way, which I think Malaysia should follow, and you just say from now on each year is going to work three months longer,” he said.
How will the maths work?
Price explained how the gradual shift to the right direction of eventually hitting 65 can work, where three months are added for each of the remaining years that a worker will be working.
So if you announce that the retirement age will be 65 from 2040, anyone currently working who is below the age of 40 will retire at 65.
“But there’s a transitional period so it goes 60, 60 and 3 months, 60 and 6 months, 60 and 9 months, 61 so it’s gradually going year by year,” he said.
For example, a 40-year-old would have 20 years’ time to prepare and adjust to the idea of working five more years to retire at 65, instead of 60.
On the flip side, those nearer to the initial retirement age of 60 would not suddenly have to adjust to the idea of working until 65.
“If you’re currently 50, you’re going to retire at 62 and a half. If you’re currently 55, you’re going to retire at 61 and a bit,” he said.
For someone aged 59, they would just have to accept that they will be working three months longer, and would retire at 60 years and three months.
“So, the closer you are, the smaller the change; the further away, then you get time to put the whole change in,” he added.
Apart from being psychologically easier to accept, he said: “It’s easier for the labour market to adjust so that employers are used to hiring workers who are staying longer or who are older. And most countries try to do this, some sort of gradual phasing in of the change in retirement age.”
Price said this gradual method is less politically divisive as people would just be retiring months apart from each other, instead of there being two different groups with very different experiences of retiring at 60 and 65 respectively.
“And it’s the dominant model that countries do around the world, work out how late people need to retire, work out a pathway to adjust towards it over time gradually,” he said.
If the retirement age is increased to 65, he said it could come with caveats, where those who started working at a younger age (such as age 16) can retire earlier at around age 60, as compared to those who went to university first and started working later (such as age 26).
“So you usually have a rule where the retirement age is ‘X’ but after you’ve done say 40 years or 45 years you can retire. So that maybe it’s possible to retire a bit earlier for the people who started work for longer,” he said.
“Because often the people who work from age 16, it’s often people who are from less wealthy backgrounds, in lower-paid jobs, sometimes more physically-demanding jobs. So it makes sense … basically they’ve more than done enough years of contributions, so they should be able to retire a bit early,” he said.
Linking the retirement age to life expectancy
After increasing to 65, Price said Malaysia could ideally adopt what some countries do, which is to link retirement age to the Department of Statistics Malaysia’s (DOSM) life expectancy figures.
“And so if people are not living that much longer, then you don’t change your retirement age. If they are living that much longer, then you do,” he said when explaining that the retirement age could be further increased or stay the same depending on whether life expectancy rises.
Based on the latest DOSM figures released September 30, life expectancy for a baby born in Malaysia in 2026 has increased to 75.5, while those aged 60 now are expected to live 20.2 years more (age 80.2) and those aged 65 now are expected to live 16.5 years more (age 81.5).
Linking the retirement age to access to retirement funds, with built-in flexibilities
Price said most people would not have sufficient income until they die, saying: “So they need to work longer, they need to save longer, and they need to take their money later.”
To make this work, Price also proposed linking the gradual increase in retirement age to a similar gradual increase of the age to access retirement savings, using a similar transition method.
He said it would be psychologically and politically difficult if those expecting to access their retirement funds at 55 were suddenly told they could only access it at 65.
Instead, workers who are 20 years away from retiring could have the age they access their retirement savings increased to 65, which would match the new retirement age.
At the same time, he said there could still be some flexibility, where those who have saved more in their EPF could be granted “early access” to the extra amount beyond the basic savings level. He said this could be an incentive to encourage people to save more.
The EPF’s guide for what Malaysians can target to save up by retirement has three levels to aim for, currently: basic savings at (RM390,000), adequate savings (RM650,000) and enhanced savings (RM1.3 million).
An older person may work differently than in their youth
During an ISWC 2026 panel session, Price noted some may mistakenly fear that a higher retirement age would mean older people do not leave their jobs and that it would lead to higher youth unemployment rates.
But he described this as the “lump of labour fallacy”, which refers to the mistaken belief that there is only a fixed number of jobs available.
“The evidence suggests, good labour markets which have the ability for employers to offer jobs, show the opposite,” he said, adding that raising the retirement age could be done without increasing unemployment for those in their 20s and 30s.
Price said the biggest benefit of working longer would be to fund retirement, as it would mean more years of not needing to tap or rely solely on one’s retirement savings.
He said older persons may not necessarily continue working full time or the same jobs until they hit age 65; and that where and how they work and the number of working hours or days could change.
“But if you’re working three days a week when you’re 62 to [63, 64, 65], drawing down a little bit of your assets, that gives you enough income. That means that you’re not wiping out everything in that first 10 years or so,” he said in his ISWC presentation.
Licensed financial planner Rajen Devadason said political will is required for Malaysia to increase its retirement age. — Sayuti Zainudin
Raise it to 65 by 2030, 70 by 2050
Licensed financial planner Rajen Devadason said it is time for Malaysia to gradually move up its current retirement age of 60, which he feels is “too low”, and said this will require political will as it can be politically unpalatable.
“I think that Malaysia’s retirement age should be shifted up, obviously in stages, to 65 by the year 2035, and to 70 by the year 2050,” he told
Malay Mail
in an interview at the ISWC 2026.
In his hypothetical example, Rajen said the retirement age could be increased by one year every two years (or in other words, by one month every two months).
While saying that a mandatory higher retirement age would “work better”, Rajen said people would be more willing to accept the change if they are given an option on whether to retire later.
Higher retirement ages won’t deprive younger workers of jobs
Rajen acknowledged resistance by some against higher retirement ages: “A lot of people get very upset. They say, ‘If you are older and you work longer, you will then be depriving younger people of jobs.’ I don’t think that’s true.”
“Because you think about it. By the time someone is 55, 60, and then if he or she keeps working till 65, 70, etc., the jobs that that particular individual is doing would be very, very different from the jobs that younger people entering the workforce would be doing.
“So, what is required is economic growth and the ability to actually create enough jobs,” he said.
“But it’s going to be a tough journey, because not just in Malaysia, in every country, people resist being told that you are required to retire later. People resent it,” he said.
But for those who might not want to retire later even if they have the option to do so, Rajen indicated the reality — especially for private sector employees — would be running out of funds during retirement: “You don’t want to work, don’t work. You’ll just run out of money.”
At ISWC 2026, Rajen had also pointed out that people are increasingly living longer, such as his oldest client who died at 103, Tun Dr Hasmah Mohamad Ali at 100, and his own mother at over 94.
“Our legislation is caught in a time warp. And the set retirement age at 60 is irrationally low in my opinion. And if you retire at 60 and the average lifespan is 75, you assume, okay, you’ve only got 15 years to go.
“But the trouble with averages is that they actually hide half, half the people who live longer,” he said, when explaining that living longer also meant planning to ensure sufficient income in the remaining years.
Rajen said Malaysians would need to have the right skills required by an evolving global marketplace in order to work longer and work remotely here, saying that they could start preparing from young by mastering languages such as English, Mandarin and Spanish as well as focusing on Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics (STEM) courses.
International Labour Organisation (ILO) Senior Social Protection Specialist for South Asia Mariko Ouchi suggested a flexible range for retirement ages, as some may want to work longer while some have to retire earlier. — Picture by Sayuti Zainudin
Working longer gives meaning too, but some may have to retire earlier
International Labour Organisation (ILO) Senior Social Protection Specialist for South Asia Mariko Ouchi said one solution could be allowing flexibility in the retirement age, saying for example that it could be fixed at a range of age 60 to 65.
Ouchi said some people may want to work longer as the income from employment is usually higher than from pensions or old-age benefits, and that those who are healthy may want to continue working for reasons beyond money and as work has meaning for them.
As for those who have health concerns or have to take care of older parents or other family responsibilities, she said they could still retire at 60 but possibly receive less old-age benefits compared to those who work longer and continue contributing more years.
“So, you know, like for those who agree for the later retirement, keep some options for them to retire a little bit later,” she said during an ISWC 2026 panel session, adding that the retirement age could be increased gradually such as by three months or six months per year.
ILO Regional Social Protection Specialist for South-East Asia and the Pacific André Gama (first one from the left) said younger and older workers can complement each other’s strengths when working together. — Picture by Firdaus Latif
Introduce policies against age discrimination at workplace
ILO Regional Social Protection Specialist for South-East Asia and the Pacific André Gama said retirement ages have to be increased gradually to enable people to adjust, adding that such increases can “mimic” the increase in life expectancy.
“For those workers who want to continue to work or will need to continue to work above the retirement age, what are the policies we need?
“Well, we need gradual increases in retirement ages in most countries. It is unavoidable, it is unpopular, but it’s a necessity,” he said during his IWSC 2026 presentation.
Gama said global data showed workers older than 65 were more likely to be doing agriculture work which tends to be more physically demanding, and were also more likely to be doing informal work, and less likely to be doing high-skilled jobs despite having more experience.
“If we don’t act, if there’s no policies in place to address this, we see that older people will struggle in the labour market,” he said, adding that policies are needed to ensure older people are treated with dignity at the workplace.
Gama said there needs to be more “age-inclusive” policies for the labour market, as older workers tend to have less rights, face discrimination and face obstacles in being able to contribute to their full potential.
Noting some employers may think older workers are more likely to be sick or might quit in a few years’ time, Gama pointed out there are existing policies preventing workplace discrimination, such as against women based on their likelihood to become pregnant.
He proposed incentives such as subsidies for hiring older workers, adding that their experience could complement younger workers.
He gave a hypothetical example where a 60-year-old policeman may not be able to run after a thief very fast, while a 20-year-old policeman may lack experience to communicate and diffuse the situation when a nervous thief pointing a gun.
“But if you have the two of them working together, then you can get the best of both worlds,” he said, adding that some jobs and work responsibilities could be adjusted to take full advantage of older workers’ experience and also account for some limitations.
“But we need to look at this in a more proactive way, and not just think that the market by itself, and the private sector by purely the magic invisible hand of economics is going to provide them the incentives to do so,” he said.

Title: Haze: Education Ministry coordinating school operating procedures under new action plan
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 14 — The Ministry of Education (MOE) has begun coordinating school operating procedures based on the National Haze Action Plan (PTJK) to ensure that decisions on school closures are made in a more systematic manner, taking into account Air Pollutant Index (API) readings and health advice.
Its minister, Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek, said that under the coordinated procedures, outdoor activities would be postponed when the API reading exceeds 100, while schools would be closed when the reading exceeds 200, in accordance with the PTJK.
“We need to understand that API readings can change within a short period.
“Closing schools several days in advance without taking these changes into account could result in children losing learning time even after air quality has returned to normal,” she said in a Facebook post today.
She said the ministry welcomed the National Disaster Management Agency’s (NADMA) emphasis that haze management must be guided by the PTJK, following discussions with relevant agencies.
At the same time, Fadhlina said she understood the concerns of parents who have to wait for daily decisions on school operations while the country faces haze, particularly those whose children have health problems or are more sensitive to air pollution.
As such, she said parents could keep their children at home if they were concerned about their health and safety during the haze, provided they notify the school authorities.
“The safety and health of our children remain our top priority. However, every school day also matters for their development and learning.
“I hope this coordination will provide greater certainty for parents, reduce the difficulties they face and ensure that every decision on school operations takes into account both the health of children and the continuity of their education in a balanced manner,” she added. — Bernama

Title: PM Anwar extends donation to Makkal Osai senior editor
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 (Bernama) — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has extended a donation to
Makkal Osai
senior editor Rajan Boopalan, who is undergoing treatment at Selayang Hospital after suffering a blood clot in his head.
Anwar said several officers from the Prime Minister’s Office had visited Rajan at the hospital on his behalf.
“Besides enquiring about his condition and conveying my regards, they also handed over a contribution on my behalf to ease the burden on him and his family during his treatment,” Anwar said in a Facebook post today.
He also prayed for Rajan’s speedy recovery and for his treatment to proceed smoothly.
Anwar expressed hope that Rajan would fully recover and that his family would be given the strength to get through this challenging period.
Rajan was previously reported to have been found unconscious at his home before further examinations confirmed that a blood vessel in his head had ruptured.
He subsequently underwent a surgical procedure to remove the blood clot, and his condition is now reported to be stable as he receives further treatment. — bernama

Title: Malay Rulers urge outsiders not to politicise Negeri Sembilan throne dispute
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 —The Malay Rulers have urged outsiders not to interfere in or politicise the dispute over the Negeri Sembilan throne, calling for the matter to be resolved by the relevant authorities through proper legal and customary channels.
In a statement issued today by Keeper of the Rulers’ Seal Tan Sri Syed Danial Syed Ahmad on behalf of the Malay Rulers, all parties involved were urged to exercise wisdom, patience and respect for adab, adat and the dignity of the royal institution.
“The issue must never be exploited for political gain, to garner support, expand influence or advance agendas in a power struggle.
“Contradictory and irresponsible statements will only worsen the situation, heighten tensions, confuse the public and tarnish the dignity of the royal institution,” the statement read.
The Malay Rulers also called for differences to be resolved through legitimate and authoritative channels, guided by consultation, consensus, adat and the provisions of the Laws of the Constitution of Negeri Sembilan 1959.
“Opportunities for dialogue must be pursued sincerely to achieve a dignified resolution without belittling or humiliating any party,” the statement said.
The Malay Rulers also stressed that the throne was a position of trust carrying immense responsibility towards the state and its people.
As efforts to resolve the dispute continue, the Malay Rulers urged all parties to preserve family ties, social harmony and respect for the royal institution while avoiding statements or actions that could aggravate tensions.
The statement warned that comments or actions made without a proper understanding of Negeri Sembilan’s customs, history and constitutional framework could undermine public harmony.
“The public is also urged not to spread unverified information or be influenced by narratives that could divide society.
“Allow the relevant authorities the time and space to discharge their duties and responsibilities with wisdom and sound judgement,” it said.
The Malay Rulers also prayed that Allah would grant all parties the wisdom to rise above emotions and place consensus above disagreement.
“Negeri Sembilan’s interests, public harmony and the dignity of the royal institution must come first.
“In circumstances such as these, the best course is to observe proper conduct, respect the adat, exercise restraint in speech and refrain from interfering in matters beyond one’s authority,” the statement said. — Bernama

Title: Tuanku Muhriz: Royal succession disputes must follow adat, law
Article:
KUALA PILAH, Oct 14 — Disputes over royal succession in Negeri Sembilan must be resolved in accordance with adat or customary law and legal provisions, rather than personal interests, Yang Dipertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir said today.
His Royal Highness stressed that the authority of the royal institution must be upheld through integrity, justice and responsibility, warning that actions contrary to established customs could undermine public confidence and threaten the state’s stability.
Tuanku Muhriz said Adat Perpatih and the law formed the foundation of the position of the Ruler and succession to the throne in Negeri Sembilan, while adat institutions, including the Undang Yang Empat, Lembaga, Ibu Soko, Buapak and Anak Buah, represented an important heritage passed down through generations to preserve traditions and maintain stability.
“Those who, over the past several months, have taken actions that sparked disputes over succession rules in the name of defending adat must understand that adat cannot be defended by violating its own rules.
“Such actions not only risk undermining the authority of customary institutions and the palace but could also destabilise the state and erode public trust,” he said in his royal address at the installation ceremony of the 17th Undang of Jelebu at Istana Besar Seri Menanti here today.
The ceremony was also attended by Tunku Ampuan Besar Negeri Sembilan Tuanku Aishah Rohani Tengku Besar Mahmud, Tunku Besar Seri Menanti Tunku Ali Redhauddin Tuanku Muhriz and Tunku Panglima Besar Tunku Zain Al-‘Abidin.
State Secretary Datuk Mohd Zafir Ibrahim and heads of state government departments were in attendance.
Tuanku Muhriz said the authority of the institution of the Ruler depends on respect for adat, the supremacy of the Constitution and the rule of law.
“The high and noble position of the Ruler comes with a great trust and responsibility. The trust of the people, in turn, is an essential foundation for ensuring that this institution continues to be respected and preserved.
“As the Malay proverb says,
Raja adil raja disembah, raja zalim raja disanggah
(a just ruler is revered, a tyrannical ruler is opposed); justice and integrity must always be the foundation of leadership.
His Royal Highness urged all parties to learn from history and not allow personal interests to override truth and justice at the expense of the state’s security, well-being and longstanding heritage.
Tuanku Muhriz said adat is not merely a heritage to take pride in, but a trust that must be preserved and defended with full responsibility.
“Indeed, the future and stability of Negeri Sembilan depend on the readiness of all of us to respect adat, to obey the law, and to place the interests of the state above personal interest, for the sake of generations to come,” he said.
His Royal Highness concluded by expressing hope that Negeri Sembilan Darul Khusus continues to be at peace and prosperous, with its institution of monarchy, its adat heritage and the unity of its people always preserved. — Bernama

Title: Judgment reserved in Saifuddin Nasution’s appeal over RM600,000 awarded to Sanusi
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 14 — The Court of Appeal today reserved its judgment in Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail’s appeal against the Alor Setar High Court decision ordering him to pay RM600,000 in damages to Kedah Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor for defamation.
The defamation case concerns statements regarding rare earth elements (REE) and misappropriated funds allocated under the Malaysian Road Records Information System (MARRIS).
A three-member bench led by Judge Datuk Azhahari Kamal Ramli deferred its decision after hearing submissions from Saifuddin Nasution’s counsel Razlan Hadri Zulkifli and counsel Yusfarizal Yussoff, who represented Muhammad Sanusi.
“We have fixed Oct 16 for case management to set a date to deliver the decision,” said Justice Azhahari Kamal, who sat with Justices Datuk Ong Chee Kwan and Datuk Seri Mohd Radzi Harun.
On Aug 24, 2025, the Alor Setar High Court allowed Muhammad Sanusi’s suit against Saifuddin Nasution after finding the latter liable for defamation.
The court awarded Muhammad Sanusi RM600,000 in global damages, comprising general, aggravated and exemplary damages, plus RM70,000 in costs.
Earlier, Razlan Hadri submitted that if the court found that either statement did not convey the actionable meaning on which the High Court had imposed liability, Muhammad Sanusi’s claim in respect of that statement should be dismissed.
“If a narrower defamatory meaning survives, justification and fair comment fall to be determined against that narrower meaning and the factual substratum established in the evidence,” he said.
Meanwhile, Yusfarizal contended that the finding was consistent with Muhammad Sanusi’s own submissions at the High Court, where it was argued that political success was not a measure of reputational harm in a defamation action.
“The High Court judge had expressly and unreservedly accepted that submission. The appellant’s (Saifuddin Nasution) submission on appeal, if accepted, would mean that no successful politician could ever recover for defamation, which is not and has never been the law.
“I respectfully submit that the appeal ought to be dismissed with costs, and the High Court’s decision, including the awards of damages and the ancillary relief granted, ought to be affirmed in its entirety,” he said.
On Aug 3, 2023, Muhammad Sanusi filed a lawsuit against Saifuddin Nasution, alleging that the defendant had spoken to the press after an official event in Penang on July 14 the same year.
He claimed Saifuddin Nasution made the MARRIS statement at that press conference, alleging in substance that the plaintiff had used funds allocated under the system, statutorily earmarked for road maintenance, for development purposes.
Muhammad Sanusi, who is the Jeneri MP, said Saifuddin Nasution made the statement during an election rally on July 15, 2023, at Padang Awam, Guar Chempedak, Yan, alleging that he had stolen REE. — Bernama

Title: Creative content drive must be matched by child online safety measures, says Fahmi
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — Efforts to promote creative content on digital platforms must go hand in hand with measures to protect children from online sexual crimes, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said.
He said this was necessary to support the government’s aspiration to strengthen the country’s creative economy through the production of quality and responsible digital content.
“We want to encourage the production of creative content, including on platforms such as YouTube. However, our challenge is to prevent crimes such as online child sexual exploitation and grooming.
“Our priority is to prevent children from using these platforms to communicate with adults who may seek to exploit them,” he told reporters after attending the Creators for Impact 2026 programme here today.
Fahmi said the Communications Ministry and the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) continued to encourage creative content production, including on digital platforms, as part of efforts to strengthen the country’s creative economy.
He said the Orange Economy Council, established to oversee policies and review programmes related to the creative economy, also supported efforts to develop the sector.
On the ‘Creators for Impact 2026’ programme organised by Google, Fahmi said the initiative exposed content creators to techniques for producing relevant content while incorporating online safety messages for audiences.
Earlier, in his speech, he said content creators could play a greater role in promoting responsible internet use among young people through engaging and relevant content.
He said closer cooperation between the government, technology companies and content creators was essential to ensure digital safety messages reached young people effectively. — Bernama

Title: Negeri Sembilan JPJ impounds four luxury cars driven by unlicensed foreigners
Article:
SEREMBAN, Oct 14 —The Negeri Sembilan Road Transport Department (JPJ) seized four luxury vehicles driven by non-citizens under Op Luxury PeWA, an operation targeting foreign drivers who violate road transport laws.
State JPJ director Jasyindar Singh Sihdu said the vehicles comprised a Toyota Vellfire, two Mercedes-Benz A250s and a BMW limousine, driven by Bangladeshi, Pakistani, Chinese and Myanmar nationals aged between 30 and 40.
“The drivers were detained for not having valid driving licences or insurance, while their vehicles also had no valid road tax,” he told a press conference at the JPJ Seizure Depot here today.
According to him, 498 of 3,741 vehicles driven by foreign nationals were seized under the Foreign Driver Operation (Op PeWA) in Negeri Sembilan from Jan 1 to Oct 11 this year.
He said 2,422 summonses were issued during the operation, while 288 notices were recorded under Section 64(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987, which empowers authorities to seize motor vehicles in specified circumstances.
Of the vehicles seized, 313 were motorcycles, 149 were cars and 36 were goods vehicles.
Jasyindar said the drivers involved were from Pakistan, Myanmar, Thailand, Indonesia, India, Bangladesh and other countries.
“Investigations found that many used their vehicles for work, such as selling bread and ice cream or operating grass-cutting machines, while most were without valid driving licences and had expired road tax,” he said.
He said last year, 4,811 vehicles were inspected and action was taken against 746, while 3,287 summonses were issued and 301 notices were recorded under Section 64(1). — Bernama

Title: Police arrest 29 men over alleged spread of banned groups’ propaganda on social media
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — Police have arrested 29 men, including a foreigner, on suspicion of promoting and spreading propaganda related to illegal organisations on social media.
Bukit Aman Criminal Investigation Department (CID) director Datuk M. Kumar said the suspects, aged 18 to 49, were arrested under Ops Mega TikTok 2026, conducted from Oct 10-12.
He said the operation to monitor the activities of associations declared illegal by the government was carried out in collaboration with the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC).
“As a result of the operation, involving 11 police contingents in Selangor, Johor, Pahang, Penang, Perak, Kuala Lumpur, Negeri Sembilan, Kedah, Melaka, Sabah and Sarawak, 28 Malaysians and a foreigner were arrested,” he said in a statement today.
Kumar said all the suspects have been remanded under Section 117 of the Criminal Procedure Code to determine their roles in the group and possible involvement in other criminal activities.
The case is being investigated under Sections 47 and 43 of the Societies Act 1966 for offences related to possession of propaganda materials and membership in unlawful organisations, as well as under Section 6(1)(c) of the Immigration Act 1959/63 regarding the foreign suspect.
The case is also investigated under Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998 for improper use of network facilities or services
Meanwhile, he warned that police would take firm and uncompromising action against those who deliberately shared video recordings that could cause public concern.
He also advised the public to channel information on suspected organised criminal activities to the police via official channels or at the nearest police station. — Bernama

Title: Police: BYD driver to be charged over fatal Jalan Kuching crash
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — The driver of a BYD Seal involved in a six-vehicle collision that killed a five-year-old girl on Jalan Kuching is to be charged at the Magistrates Court tomorrow.
Kuala Lumpur Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Department chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Zamzuri Mohd Isa said the investigation team arrested the 24-year-old suspect immediately after he was discharged from a private hospital, where he had sought treatment.
“The suspect was arrested at about 11.30am today and is now being held at the Dang Wangi police lockup.
“The investigation papers were subsequently referred to the Attorney General’s Chambers, which agreed that the suspect would face three separate charges,” he said in a statement here.
Mohd Zamzuri said the suspect would be charged under Sections 41(1), 42(1) and 52(1) of the Road Transport Act for causing death by dangerous or reckless driving, dangerous or reckless driving, and failing to stop after an accident, respectively.
In the accident on October 10, a five-year-old girl died after the car she was travelling in was involved in the collision on Jalan Kuching heading from the city centre towards Segambut.
Preliminary police investigations found that the Perodua Bezza carrying the child and her family was struck from behind by a BYD Seal.
The Bezza then spun into the right lane and collided with three other vehicles.

Title: Tuanku Muhriz: Customs cannot be defended by breaching the rules
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan Tuanku Muhriz Ibni Almarhum Tuanku Munawir today said customs cannot be defended by breaking the very rules of custom, in a pointed address directed at those who have disputed the rules of succession in recent months.
Speaking at Istana Besar Seri Menanti this afternoon to mark the investiture of the 17th Undang of Luak Jelebu, Tuanku Muhriz said Negeri Sembilan’s constitutional monarchy, adat and legal provisions must be upheld together.
“The system of constitutional monarchy in Malaysia... places the Ruler as Head of State. However, His powers are subject to the Constitution and the law, and he serves as an umbrella of unity and a guarantor of the stability of governance,” he said.
“The dignity of the institution of the Ruler must be preserved on the basis of integrity, justice and responsibility.”
In Negeri Sembilan, he said, Adat Perpatih and legal provisions form the basis of the position and succession of the throne. The customary institutions comprising the Undang Yang Empat, Lembaga, Ibu Soko, Buapak and anak buah are an inherited legacy that is vital in safeguarding custom and ensuring the state’s stability.
Disputes must follow custom and law
The Yamtuan further said the customary system must continue to be strengthened to remain relevant with the times, without neglecting its founding principles and rules. Any dispute over the position or succession of the throne, he stressed, must be settled according to the relevant custom and law, not according to personal interests or wishes.
Without naming any party, Tuanku Muhriz said those who in recent months had taken action that gave rise to disputes over the order of succession, on the grounds of defending custom, must understand that custom cannot be defended by violating its own rules.
Such actions, he warned, could damage the standing of the customary and royal institutions, endanger the state’s stability and erode public trust.
The Ruler said the dignity of the monarchy depends on respect for custom, the supremacy of the Constitution and the rule of law. The Ruler’s exalted position, he said, comes with great trust and responsibility, and the people’s confidence is key to ensuring the institution continues to be respected and preserved.
Quoting the Malay proverb “Raja adil raja disembah, raja zalim raja disanggah” (a just ruler is revered; an unjust ruler is opposed), he said justice and integrity must always be the foundation of leadership.
Let history be a guide
Tuanku Muhriz urged Negeri Sembilan citizens to take history as a guide and lesson, and not to let self-interest override truth and justice to the point where security, well-being and a heritage safeguarded across generations are sacrificed.
Custom, he said, is not merely a heritage to be proud of but a trust that must be preserved and defended responsibly.
The future and stability of Negeri Sembilan depend on everyone’s willingness to respect custom, obey the law and place the state’s interests above personal interests for the sake of future generations, he added.

Title: Public Services Commission awaits circular on RM2,500 starting salary for fresh grads entering public service
Article:
KUALA KANGSAR, Oct 14 — The implementation of the RM2,500 starting salary for fresh graduates entering the public service, announced in Budget 2027, is pending an official circular outlining the implementation details.
Malaysian Public Services Commission (SPA) chairman and Judicial and Legal Service Commission (SPKP) chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Jailani Muhamed Yunus said the details would include the implementation timeline and related payment components.
“We welcome the announcement made in the Budget, but its implementation will have to follow the procedures stipulated in the circular.
“More detailed procedures are needed, including how the initiative will be implemented and its timeline,” he told reporters after officiating at the handover of assets under the SPA Madani Adopted School programme at Sekolah Menengah Kebangsaan Simpang Beluru here today.
He said preparations for implementing initiatives announced in the budget usually began in the year of the announcement to enable implementation the following year.
Asked whether the RM2,500 amount included other allowances, Ahmad Jailani said the matter would be reviewed and clarified in the official circular.
He said detailed consideration was necessary as the initiative involved a substantial financial allocation and a large number of beneficiaries.
“This matter must be handled carefully and systematically. I am confident that the relevant parties have done their work and that the matter can be resolved satisfactorily,” he said. — Bernama
