Title: Malaysia gives Nepal US$1m in flood relief aid
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 14 — Malaysia has handed over US$1 million (RM4.08 million) in humanitarian assistance to Nepal to support relief and recovery efforts following devastating floods that struck the country on August 26.
Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan presented the contribution to Nepal’s Chargé d’Affaires in Kuala Lumpur, Mudita Bajracharya, at a ceremony here on Wednesday, according to the Foreign Ministry, also known as Wisma Putra.
“The contribution reflects Malaysia’s unwavering support for the government and people of Nepal during this difficult time,” Wisma Putra said in a statement.
Mohamad also conveyed Malaysia’s deepest sympathies and heartfelt condolences to the government and people of Nepal, particularly to the families who lost their loved ones and all those affected by the disaster, it said.
Wisma Putra said Mohamad welcomed the Nepalese government's approval of a new ordinance concerning the declaration of death of victims who remain uncontactable, which reduces the applicable period from 12 years to 45 days from the date of the disaster.
“The new ordinance will provide greater legal and administrative certainty for affected families,” Wisma Putra said.
The ministry said Nepal’s Chargé d’Affaires in Kuala Lumpur conveyed that the details of the ordinance and its modalities were being finalised by the government of Nepal.
“Malaysia stands in solidarity with the government and people of Nepal throughout the recovery and reconstruction process and reaffirms its support for international humanitarian efforts in the aftermath of the disaster,” the ministry said. — Bernama

Title: Haze: Schools in Selangor, Negeri Sembilan, Melaka, Pahang to reopen tomorrow
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — Educational institutions under the Ministry of Education (MOE) in Selangor, Negeri Sembilan, Melaka and Pahang will reopen tomorrow.
The Selangor State Education Department said school operations in the state will prioritise the safety, health and well-being of pupils and school staff.
“Pupils are encouraged to wear face masks as a precaution. Parents or guardians who are concerned about their children’s health amid the haze may choose not to send them to school.
“However, they must notify the school if their children will be absent,” it said in a statement today.
In Negeri Sembilan, the state Education Department reminded schools to monitor air quality regularly, comply with the guidelines in force and take appropriate measures to safeguard pupils’ health.
“Schools must suspend all outdoor activities, including Physical Education lessons, co-curricular activities, sports, camping, celebrations, assemblies and activities in open halls, when the Air Pollutant Index (API) reading exceeds 100,” the department said.
The Melaka State Education Department said educational institutions under MOE will resume operations tomorrow, pending official confirmation of the latest API readings.
The department urged administrators to take appropriate measures to ensure smooth operations and comply with the ministry’s directives, while immediately suspending all outdoor activities and assemblies.
“Students are encouraged to wear face masks and drink water regularly. Parents and guardians are advised to continue monitoring their children’s health and seek medical attention if they develop symptoms related to air pollution.
“Any changes to the operating instructions will be announced on the official Melaka State Education Department Facebook page,” the statement said.
Schools in Pekan, Kuantan, Rompin, Temerloh, Maran, Bera and Bentong in Pahang will also reopen tomorrow, the State Education Department said.
Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek yesterday announced the closure of all schools in Johor, Melaka and Negeri Sembilan, as well as several districts in Selangor, Pahang, Sabah and Sarawak, today due to haze. — Bernama

Title: Parliament’s new service council to be fully operational by December, says Dewan Rakyat Speaker
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — The Parliamentary Service Council (MPP), which will oversee the administrative autonomy of the Malaysian Parliament, is expected to be fully operational by December.
Dewan Rakyat Speaker Tan Sri Johari Abdul said the council would oversee matters including the service scheme, career paths and administration of parliamentary officers, as well as ensure compliance with the provisions of the Parliamentary Services Act 2025.
“We hope the establishment of the MPP, beginning in December, will enable Parliament to restore the principle of separation of powers and strengthen the country’s democracy in accordance with the mandate of the Federal Constitution,” he told a press conference after the handover ceremony marking administrative transition and institutional reform at the Malaysian Parliament here today.
The event was attended by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, Dewan Negara President Senator Datuk Seri Awang Bemee Awang Ali Basah, Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar and Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said.
Johari said the establishment of the MPP followed the official enforcement of the Parliamentary Services Act 2025 on October 1, restoring Parliament’s administrative independence after 33 years under the Prime Minister’s Department (JPM).
He said the MPP would be co-chaired by the Dewan Rakyat Speaker and the Dewan Negara President, with a total membership of 16.
Johari said its members would include the Director-General of Public Services (KPPA), Treasury Secretary-General (KSP), four Members of Parliament and two senators, who would be elected when the Dewan Negara sitting begins on Nov 30.
At the Dewan Rakyat sitting this morning, the prime minister tabled a motion to appoint four MPs to the MPP, which was passed by a majority without debate.
The four appointees, comprising two government and two opposition representatives, are Ramkarpal Singh (PH-Bukit Gelugor), Datuk Seri Hasni Mohammad (BN-Simpang Renggam), Datuk Seri Dr Ronald Kiandee (PN-Beluran) and Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan (PN-Kota Bharu). — Bernama

Title: Weather warning: MetMalaysia puts most of the country on thunderstorm alert
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued an afternoon thunderstorm advisory, warning that heavy downpours, gusty winds, and lightning will lash widespread areas across Peninsular Malaysia, Sabah, and Sarawak until 7pm today.
The advisory places the entirety of Perlis, Penang, Kuala Lumpur, and Putrajaya on alert, alongside large swathes of the northern and central peninsula.
In Kedah, stormy weather is forecast for Kubang Pasu, Padang Terap, Sik, Baling, Kulim, and Bandar Baharu. Perak faces widespread disruption across Kerian, Selama, Hulu Perak, Kuala Kangsar, Larut Matang, Kinta, Kampar, Batang Padang, Muallim, and Bagan Datuk.
Across Selangor, the warning blankets Sabak Bernam, Kuala Selangor, Hulu Selangor, Gombak, Petaling, Hulu Langat, and Sepang. Further south, the alert covers Jempol in Negeri Sembilan and Segamat in Johor.
East coast states are similarly braced for severe weather. Kelantan will see storms hit Tanah Merah, Kuala Krai, Machang, Pasir Mas, Tumpat, Kota Bharu, Pasir Puteh, and Bachok. In Terengganu, bad weather is expected across Hulu Terengganu, Besut, Dungun, Kemaman, and Setiu, while Pahang residents in Kuantan, Maran, Jerantut, Bera, and Rompin have also been advised to brace for rain.
Across East Malaysia, the warning stretches across multiple divisions in Sarawak. These include Kuching, Serian and Siburan, Samarahan, Sri Aman, Betong, Sarikei (incorporating Julau), Sibu, Mukah (covering Daro, Matu, and Dalat), Kapit (including Song), Miri (featuring Marudi and Beluru), and Limbang.
In Sabah, the alert spans the interior divisions of Sipitang, Beaufort, Membakut, and Tambunan, before extending across the West Coast through Papar, Penampang, Kota Kinabalu, Tuaran, and Kota Belud. Other affected areas in the state include Kota Marudu in Kudat, Kinabatangan in Sandakan, and Kunak in Tawau.
MetMalaysia issues thunderstorm warnings whenever rain clouds show signs of dumping more than 20mm of rain per hour, or when high-intensity downpours are imminent and likely to persist beyond an hour.
The department noted that these warnings serve as short-term alerts, with each issuance remaining valid for a maximum of six hours.

Title: Nhaveen murder trial: Prosecution cites contradictions in four accused’s defence
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Oct 14 — The High Court here was told today that there are four main grounds for the prosecution’s bid to convict the four accused in the murder of teenager T. Nhaveen nine years ago, with the contention that the defence failed to raise reasonable doubt against its case.
Deputy Public Prosecutor (DPP) Mohd Amril Johari said among these grounds was the contradiction between the defence’s version during the prosecution’s case and the accused’s testimony at the defence stage last week.
He said the defence of all four accused had shifted when they gave evidence themselves, particularly regarding a claim by one of them, who was a teenager at the time of the incident, that he was beaten unconscious with a helmet by Nhaveen’s friend, T. Previin, while trying to break up a fight.
Mohd Amril described the claim as an afterthought, as it had not been raised earlier, and said the contradictions in the accused’s testimony raised questions over the defence’s credibility.
“The defence’s case at the prosecution stage is totally different from the defence now. So, they are shifting the goalposts.
“The prosecution’s theory also does not dispute their (the accused’s) presence at both locations — Jalan Kaki Bukit and Padang Openg, Gelugor,” he said while submitting during the defence proceedings of the four individuals charged with Nhaveen’s murder.
He questioned the absence of a medical report to support the accused’s claim of being injured to the point of losing consciousness.
He also noted that the issue of a phone call made by one of the accused, J. Ragesuthen, 27, to Nhaveen’s mother, T. Shanti, on the night of the incident was supported by witness testimony.
Mohd Amril asked the court to examine the difference between the brief grounds of judgment of the Court of Appeal, which ordered the four accused to enter their defence, and the full grounds of judgment in the appeal involving another respondent, S. Gopinaath, 35, who was acquitted and discharged.
However, lawyer Maanveer Singh Dhillon, representing all four accused, argued that reasonable doubt remains over how and where the injuries that led to Nhaveen’s death occurred.
He said Nhaveen was still alive after the incident at Jalan Kaki Bukit and had ridden a motorcycle with an individual known as “Belang,” but what happened afterwards could not be ascertained based on the evidence presented in court.
He said the testimony of prosecution witnesses and medical evidence must be assessed as a whole, including the question of whether the injuries Nhaveen sustained occurred at the scene of the fight or after he was taken away.
Maanveer Singh also questioned the discrepancy in the number of individuals said to have been involved in the incident based on several versions of testimony, and stressed that the defence did not deny a scuffle had taken place at Jalan Kaki Bukit, but disputed whether that incident caused Nhaveen’s death.
Judge Datuk Mohd Radzi Abdul Hamid then set November 16 for case management to allow the prosecution and defence to file additional submissions before a decision date is fixed.
The four accused, Ragesuthan, S. Gokulan, 27, and two others who were teenagers at the time of the incident, gave their witness statements on October 8 and 9 last year.
They were charged under Section 302 of the Penal Code for Nhaveen’s murder, which carries the death penalty or imprisonment of 30 to 40 years and not less than 12 strokes of the cane, upon conviction.
They were also charged under Section 326 of the same law for voluntarily causing grievous hurt to Previin with dangerous weapons, which provides for up to 20 years’ imprisonment and a fine or caning.
Nhaveen and Previin were 18 and 19 years old, respectively, at the time of the incident.
In addition to Mohd Amril, DPPs Yazid Mustaqim Roslan and Noor Azura Zulkiflee also appeared for the prosecution, while all four accused are represented by lawyers Maanveer Singh, R. Thevan and Lim Sheng Zhe. Lawyer T. Gunaseelan is holding a watching brief for Nhaveen’s family.
Previously, the Court of Appeal ordered Ragesuthan, Gokulan and the two teenagers to enter their defence on the charge of murdering Nhaveen after allowing the prosecution’s appeal against the High Court decision that acquitted them on October 3, 2023.
They were also ordered to enter their defence on the charge of injuring Previin near the Karpal Singh Learning Centre at Jalan Kaki Bukit, Gelugor, between 11pm and midnight on June 9, 2017.
Nhaveen died on June 15, 2017, after six days of treatment at Penang Hospital from severe injuries sustained in the incident. — Bernama

Title: Five govt buildings get solar installations ahead of schedule, says works minister
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 14 — Five grid-connected photovoltaic (GCPV) solar installation projects at government buildings have been completed ahead of schedule, with a combined installed capacity of 779.86 kilowatts, Works Minister Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi said.
He said two of the projects were at Ministry of Foreign Affairs premises, while the other three were at the National Water Research Institute of Malaysia (Nahrim), Hospital Canselor Tuanku Muhriz (HCTM) and the Department of Irrigation and Drainage (DID).
“This is a concrete step towards expanding the use of clean energy at government premises, while reducing operating costs and supporting more sustainable public asset management,” he said at a ceremony to hand over the projects to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and three other government premises here today.
He said the Public Works Department (JKR) had also implemented grid-connected photovoltaic and off-grid solar installations involving 46 Federal Government buildings, 283 rural schools in Sabah, Sarawak and Peninsular Malaysia, four Royal Malaysia Police border posts and an Orang Asli village.
“These projects have the potential to generate energy cost savings of up to RM115 million annually compared with conventional electricity supplies,” he said.
Nanta said the government-building solar installation programme, led by the Ministry of Economy, received an allocation of RM57.6 million, with an initial target of installing nine megawatts of capacity in Peninsular Malaysia.
As of last September, eight projects involving 23 buildings with a capacity of 5.8 megawatts had completed their Defects Liability Period (DLP), while seven projects involving 11 buildings with a capacity of 2.09 megawatts remained within the period.
He said three other projects involving 11 buildings with a capacity of 1.29 megawatts were under construction, while another project involving one building, with a capacity of 0.5 megawatts, was at the procurement stage.
“When all the systems are fully operational, the programme is projected to generate about 13,200 megawatt-hours of electricity annually, with potential gross savings of around RM5.5 million a year on government electricity bills,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Why should a good man go when the corrupt stay? Anwar says Malaysia needs ministers like Anthony Loke
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 14 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim sought again today to make a case for Transport Minister Anthony Loke Siew Fook to remain in his Cabinet, saying the country needs principled leaders and that the corrupt should be the ones stepping down.
Speaking at the Transport Ministry during the distribution of RM1,000 special financial assistance to taxi, rental car, and school bus drivers, Anwar commended Loke's dedication to ordinary working Malaysians, including the initiative today.
“Some people think people like him should step down. Why should a good person like him have to resign? The ones who should resign are those involved in corruption,” he said in his speech.
“I told him to stay on and get the job done, because the country needs principled leaders. This country needs leaders who care about ordinary people,” he said, noting that leaders must stay focused on the daily struggles of fishermen, farmers, and low-wage workers.
Loke, who is the DAP secretary-general, tendered his resignation as transport minister on September 19 following the political controversy surrounding the conditional royal pardon granted to former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak.
Loke subsequently clarified on September 29 that he would continue serving until the issue of Najib's proposed house arrest is resolved.
Record plate sales fund driver aid
Today’s ceremony marked the immediate rollout of the RM1,000 one-off grant announced under Budget 2027 last Friday. The initiative is funded entirely by revenue generated from the Transport Ministry's special 'H' vehicle registration series, which netted RM91.2 million, far eclipsing initial projections of RM30 million.
The series set a national record for the most expensive vehicle registration number in Malaysian history, with H1 selling for RM10 million.
“The car is not included; it is just the number plate,” Loke said, in apparent jest. “This is the highest amount ever paid for a single vehicle registration number in our country.”
Loke explained that he proposed channelling the auction proceeds to public transport drivers during a working trip to Sarawak.
“I knew the prime minister had a soft spot for taxi drivers. When I made the proposal, he said, ‘Good idea, go ahead’,” Loke said.
Around 500 drivers received the RM1,000 aid vouchers at today's event to help offset operating overheads and vehicle maintenance.
The ministry will expand distribution nationwide in phases, beginning in Penang on October 17, with early disbursements timed to assist Hindu drivers ahead of the upcoming Deepavali festival.

Title: Sarawak Education Dept: Schools open tomorrow, outdoor activities halted if API tops 100
Article:
KUCHING, Oct 14 — All schools and educational institutions under the Ministry of Education (MOE) in Sarawak will operate as usual tomorrow, despite the ongoing haze affecting several areas in the state.
In a statement today, the Sarawak Education Department (JPN) said schools in areas where the Air Pollutant Index (API) reading exceeded 100 must suspend all outdoor activities.
“Students attending school are encouraged to wear face masks as a precautionary measure amid the current haze situation.
“Parents and guardians may choose not to send their children to school if they have concerns about their health due to the haze affecting several locations in Sarawak, provided they inform the school,” the statement said.
Yesterday, the department announced the temporary closure of all primary and secondary schools under the Serian, Sri Aman and Lubok Antu District Education Offices (PPD), with Teaching and Learning at Home (PdPR) implemented during the closure. — Bernama

Title: MACC: Fighting corruption starts with rejecting bribes, reporting misconduct
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — Integrity must show up in everyday actions, including rejecting bribes, complying with regulations, and having the courage to report misconduct, so society shares responsibility in the fight against corruption.
Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) Deputy Chief Commissioner (Prevention) Datuk Azmi Kamaruzaman said building a corruption-free culture starts with honest decisions and firm personal convictions, supported by sustained commitment from all parties.
“We can progress when there is no abuse of power. The shift towards a corruption-free culture begins with our own honest decisions and firm convictions,” he said.
He was speaking at the launch of the “Program Langkah Merdeka 118, Bersama Perangi Rasuah” programme, held in conjunction with the MACC’s 59th anniversary celebration for Kuala Lumpur at Stadium Merdeka here today. The programme was organised in collaboration with Permodalan Nasional Berhad (PNB) Merdeka Ventures.
Azmi said the corruption-free pledge taken by PNB Merdeka Ventures at the event should not be merely a declaration on paper, but must serve as the foundation for a clean, transparent and ethical workplace, thereby safeguarding public trust in the organisation.
Meanwhile, Kuala Lumpur MACC director Mohamad Zakkuan Talib said the symbolic act of carrying and hoisting the MACC flag atop Merdeka 118, Malaysia’s tallest building and the world’s second tallest, reflected the commission’s determination to elevate the anti-corruption agenda and strengthen integrity without compromise.
The programme also featured a tower run involving Kuala Lumpur City Hall, the Royal Malaysia Police, the Fire and Rescue Department of Malaysia, Tenaga Nasional Berhad, the Construction Industry Development Board Malaysia and MACC officers.
Lance Corporal Muhamad Khairul Izwan Mazli from the Cheras District Police Headquarters emerged champion with a time of 32 minutes and 29 seconds, while Wan Norrazif Mohameed from the Kuala Lumpur MACC office finished second, followed by Mohd Hanief Afiq Rosnei from the Negeri Sembilan MACC office in third place.
An integrity exhibition featuring nearly 20 government and private-sector ministries and agencies was also held, with participation from the Health Ministry, Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry, Malaysian Institute of Integrity, National Anti-Drugs Agency and Dewan Bahasa dan Pustaka, among others.
Various services were offered, including health and dental screenings, account checks with the Employees Provident Fund (EPF) and the National Higher Education Fund Corporation (PTPTN), as well as Rahmah Sales, book sales and jewellery sales. — Bernama

Title: Paddy farmers who suffered yield losses from fertiliser delays may get targeted aid, says minister
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — The government will assess whether to provide targeted assistance to paddy farmers whose yields declined due to delays in fertiliser supplies, evaluating affected cases on a case-by-case basis.
Agriculture and Food Security Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu said the assessment would identify farmers who genuinely suffered losses before considering any assistance.
“We will study and discuss the issue of losses so that, if funds are available, assistance can be channelled in a targeted manner rather than universally. We are looking at those who experienced yield declines and will assess the situation on a case-by-case basis in affected areas,” he said during the question-and-answer session in the Dewan Rakyat today.
He was responding to a supplementary question from Sabri Azit (PN-Jerai) on the possibility of providing incentives to padi affected by delays in fertiliser supplies.
Mohamad said he had taken proactive steps by meeting the management of the Muda Agricultural Development Authority (Mada) to seek an explanation for the delays.
He added that he had also obtained information from the relevant officials before proposing to Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, who is also Finance Minister, that the services of suppliers who failed to fulfil their obligations be terminated.
In a separate development, Deputy Defence Minister Adly Zahari said 10 per cent of the funds collected through the Warriors’ Fund Campaign (KTP) had been allocated for investment in fixed deposits with financial institutions.
He said the strategy was aimed at generating returns to grow the fund and support assistance and welfare programmes for veterans and their dependants in need.
“As of September 22, RM1.51 million had been placed in a fixed deposit with Bank Islam Malaysia Bhd at a profit rate of 3.6 per cent, maturing on March 15, 2027.
“In addition, KTP has received an allocation of RM2 million from the Finance Ministry, and approval is pending to place the funds in a new fixed deposit to generate additional returns,” he said.
Adly was responding to a question from Nordin Ahmad Ismail (PN-Lumut) on the strategic direction of the Warriors’ Fund (Tabung Pahlawan) transformation, particularly efforts to move away from reliance on seasonal public contributions towards a sustainable fundraising model driven by strategic investments or corporate partnerships. — Bernama

Title: Foreign minister: Malaysians in Riyadh, Jeddah safe amid Saudi tensions
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 14 — Malaysians living and working in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, have been reported safe amid continuing tensions in the country, Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said.
He said daily reports from the Malaysian Embassy in Riyadh and the Malaysian Consulate in Jeddah confirmed that Malaysians in both cities were safe and well.
“I receive daily reports from our embassy in Riyadh and our consul in Jeddah confirming that Malaysians there are all right.
“The Malaysian workers there are also safe,” he told reporters after attending the handover ceremony for a solar photovoltaic (grid-connected PV) system installation project by the Works Ministry to the Foreign Ministry and three other government premises here today.
Mohamad said the embassy and consulate remained in contact with Malaysians in the respective cities to monitor their safety and well-being.
He also advised Malaysians in Saudi Arabia to stay away from public areas and strategic locations that could potentially be targeted in attacks.
“As far as possible, they should remain at home. We are also using the e-Konsular system to maintain contact with them,” he said.
Mohamad said several Malaysians in Jeddah had also been temporarily stranded following the cancellation of return flights amid operational disruptions affecting Malaysian and international airlines.
He said the security situation in Saudi Arabia remained tense following another reported attack yesterday.
The attack was reported to have targeted an Aramco complex belonging to the Saudi Arabian oil company, which operates large-scale oil refining and production facilities.
In view of the situation, Mohamad advised Malaysians without urgent reasons to travel to Saudi Arabia to postpone their trips until the security situation improved.
In a separate development, he said the ministry could provide consular assistance to Malaysians detained in Japan in connection with drug-related cases, but legal proceedings fell under the jurisdiction of the Japanese authorities.
He said Japan maintained strict confidentiality to protect the privacy of detainees, and consular visits could not be arranged without their consent.
“We cannot simply arrange a visit at the request of family members without the consent of the person detained.
“If the family wants us to conduct a consular visit to check on the detainee’s welfare or provide any necessary assistance, they should ask the detainee or the person concerned to submit a written request to the Japanese authorities,” he said.
It was reported that four Malaysian men and a woman had been detained at Haneda Airport in Tokyo last Saturday for allegedly attempting to smuggle about five kilogrammes of cocaine worth ¥120 million (RM3.1 million), concealed beneath shoe insoles.
The group was believed to have transported the drugs from Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) in Sepang before being discovered during customs checks upon arrival in Japan. — Bernama
